streams.why_this_stage_exists_and_it_is_not_the_:
The coordinator offered `verify --run-harness` as a way to MEASURE the hook's duration, and left the choice to me. I am taking it for a dearer reason: whether the nineteen PASS. Counted, not assumed - the 2026-11-01 push executed SEVEN commands (route crewing-c3b2); my route declares NINETEEN; and of those I have executed exactly ONE in this task (my own, 184 asserts green). So TWELVE would run for the first time at the moment of an irreversible action. He then verified that list independently against every guard record on disk and it matched name for name: seven have a recorded outcome, all `pass` on 2026-11-01; twelve have no recorded outcome anywhere.

MY FIRST REASON WAS STALE AND HE MEASURED WHICH PART. I argued from owner-authorised RED harness debt. Two of three legs are now gone: No.879 `stack_build_metadata` pinned 0.4.136 against a 0.4.138 house, and on my pushed bytes AND on origin/main those four asserts pin 0.4.139 while the house declares 0.4.139 in tauri.conf.json, Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock - cured by No.882/PR #76; and No.878's ghost harness `crewing_escaping_negative` exists on my sha and on origin/main - cured by PR #77. On the third, the manager's own canon (PROJECT_STATE No.876, 29.10) says presence 130 and c3b2 1 are NOT baseline red - green on base and on main - and that a BRANCH turns them red; the 2026-11-01 record shows `crewing_presence_contract` passing on d58a4a22, an ancestor of my head.

So the conclusion stands and the REASON is replaced, with his wording because it is stronger than mine: not 'one of the twelve is surely red in the house', but 'twelve have no recorded outcome for THIS task, and the only redness the canon records was caused by a BRANCH rather than by the house' - which is precisely the class my four-file change could reproduce. The local run therefore checks MY CHANGE, not the state of the house, and that is worth more than what I first claimed it was for.
streams.the_positive_control_is_unusually_clean_: Stage 6 established, on this exact base and route, that all nineteen commands read `not_run` when the flag is absent. So the proof that `--run-harness` took effect is that NONE of them still says `not_run`. Without it, 'no failures' would read identically for 'they all passed' and 'none of them ran' - the same shape as the fetch stage, where 'nothing changed' would have read identically for 'the fetch ran and brought zero' and 'the fetch never ran'. It is a gate (exit 11), not a note, and it was drilled: a stubbed instrument leaving sixteen at not_run produced exit 11 naming all sixteen.
streams.what_the_number_is_and_is_NOT: A LOWER bound on the hook's duration, and the coordinator's caveat is carried as mine: the page cache is warm here and this checkout is not fresh, while the hook creates its tree a moment before use. So a local 25 s does not promise a 25 s hook. A local FAILURE, however, does promise a refused push - which is the asymmetry that makes this stage worth a round. It will also be the first measurement of this 19-command route that anyone has: nobody has ever timed it, and bin/skipi-guard contains no perf_counter, time.time, monotonic, elapsed, duration or datetime.now, so the skipi-guard.v1 JSON cannot carry timing BY CONSTRUCTION and every duration must come from an external bracket.
streams.why_running_them_in_THIS_worktree_is_the: The hook runs the harnesses in a fresh detached worktree that mkdtemp places DIRECTLY INSIDE /home/linux/Developer/worktrees. This worktree is itself a direct child of that directory, so `../../skipi-plugins/...` from tests/ resolves through the SAME symlink (/home/linux/Developer/worktrees/skipi-plugins -> /home/linux/Developer/skipi-plugins, dated 2026-07-03) as it will from the hook's temp tree. The FORM matches and not merely the content - which is the lesson from stage 5, where a plain-clone fixture could not expose a per-worktree defect. It also creates NO new entry in the shared gitdir, unlike `git worktree add`, so it is strictly less invasive than the thing it predicts. What it does NOT reproduce: a fresh checkout's cold cache, and the hook's own base arithmetic from stdin.
streams.two_of_the_nineteen_leave_this_worktree_: The coordinator's correction, taken: my first count said one because my instrument read COMMAND LINES, and a command line does not show what the file it runs imports - the same shape as every other instrument error of mine today, where the tool was right and the object was wrong. `shared_host_runtime_isolation` leaves by its command (an absolute path into skipi-plugins). `crewing_plugin_isolation` leaves by its IMPORTS - two from ../../skipi-plugins/_host-runtime/harness/{fake-dom,isolation-contract}.mjs - plus a read of an absolute .../dist/RUNTIME_VERSION. Declared by REALPATH (/home/linux/Developer/skipi-plugins/_host-runtime) and not by the symlink spelling, for his reason: `overlaps()` compares path tokens by string equality or parenthood, and a symlink spelling is neither equal to the real path nor its parent, so declaring through the symlink would not collide with a neighbour who declared the real path. The symlink spelling belongs in notes, which is where it is. And his limit is carried too: that list comes from literal call sites, so it is a LOWER bound, not a complete one.
streams.no_harness_opens_a_socket_spawns_a_proce: Measured so that `ports` could be declared empty honestly rather than hopefully, over the 19 files resolved from the authoritative command strings. Result: no real network call, no process spawn, no file-write API (no writeFileSync, mkdirSync, rmSync, unlinkSync, appendFileSync or createWriteStream anywhere in the nineteen). Three greps matched and all three were FALSE POSITIVES, resolved by reading the context rather than trusting the hit: `crewing_crew_flow_demo` matches `fetch(` inside an assertion that the product does NOT call fetch; `crewing_trial_gate_wired` and `crewing_trial_activate_unconnected` each define a STUB `async fetch(...)` the test injects as a fake; and the `spawn` match in `crewing_c3b2_candidate` is a quoted phrase inside an assertion message about a Seafarer defect. Same lower-bound caveat as the coordinator's: literal call sites only, so a path or host built from variables is invisible to this measurement. The practical consequence is that the dirty-worktree risk is low - and the control stays anyway, because 'low' is not 'measured to be zero'.
streams.a_dirty_worktree_would_be_reported_and_N: Nineteen test programs run with cwd in this tree. If any writes, the tree is dirty and the push's own precondition refuses. The driver prints the porcelain list and exits 22 WITHOUT repairing it, for two reasons: a silent cleanup would hide WHICH command did it, and restoring another program's output is a decision rather than a step. Drilled: a stub that touches a file in the tree produced exit 22, the FINDING naming `?? harness-leftover.tmp`, and the file was still present afterwards - the control proving the driver did not quietly tidy up.
streams.the_verdict_is_the_product_so_a_failure_: `verify` returns 0 if status is pass and 1 otherwise (820), so rc 1 means at least one harness failed and rc 2+ means the instrument broke. The driver keeps them apart and, on rc 1, prints the failing names AND the tail of each failing harness's own summary before exiting 23. Drilled: a stub failing crewing635_public_settings produced exit 23 with `AssertionError: expected 185 got 184` quoted from the record. Exit 23 is the stage succeeding at its job - it is the answer I came for - and the push stage then does not happen until the red is understood.
streams.an_error_of_mine_in_preparing_this: My first sweep for network calls GUESSED harness filenames from harness NAMES (crewing_trial_gate_wired -> crewing_trial_gate_wired_harness.mjs) and reported five files MISSING. The name and the path are different objects and they differ for SEVEN of the nineteen - the real command is `node tests/trial_gate_wired_harness.mjs`. Nothing was lost because the missing-file lines were loud, but a quieter version of that mistake would have reported 'no network calls' from a sweep that never opened five of the files. Redone from the authoritative command strings in stage 6's own record: 19 of 19 resolved. The coordinator hit the identical error in his own sweep and named it himself - so it is a trap of the object, not of one reader, and the rule is to take the path from the record rather than rebuild it from the name.

The measurement says none of them uses a file-write API, which makes it unlikely, not impossible. `tests.reads` names /home/linux/Developer/skipi-plugins/_host-runtime by REALPATH because two of the nineteen reach into that house. `code.reads` lists the product paths the harnesses actually open - dist, src-tauri, presence-manifest.json - plus the shared object store that `verify` reads to compute the diff. `ports` is empty by measurement, not by hope. Empty categories mean considered, per the schema.
streams.the_threshold_is_a_protocol_floor_not_a_: His structural point, accepted: a stage whose POINT is to measure a duration must not take its window threshold from a prediction, or the prediction starts guarding the measurement meant to replace it. So 120 s here is not an expected duration - it is sized by the COST OF ERROR, which is unusually symmetric and small in both directions. Starting too late costs a lease in DRAIN_REQUIRED plus a re-run: the action is local, reversible, safely interruptible, creates no entry in the shared gitdir and leaves no /tmp record, so an overrun damages nothing. Refusing too early costs one round. With both costs cheap, the floor is set where a run of the only magnitudes anyone has recorded would finish, while admitting those magnitudes are about other routes. And the floor cannot bias the result: the wall clock is recorded whatever it turns out to be, including if it exceeds the floor. Contrast stage 8, where the cost of error is one-directional - the push cannot be taken back - and 180 s is justified from above.
streams.the_main_checkout_is_36_commits_BEHIND_a: Worth recording because it would mislead anyone measuring the house from the obvious place. `crewing_escaping_negative` does NOT exist at the main checkout's HEAD (0223bbd3), which is 36 commits behind origin/main with 0 ahead - so any check of 'does this harness exist in the house' taken from the main checkout still reports a ghost that was cured by PR #77. It exists on my pushed bytes and on origin/main, which are the objects that matter. This is the same trap as reading `head` from stage 6's record and getting the literal string 'HEAD': the field pins the object only in `sha`, and only to seven characters. The push's own record will be better - pre_push_ref passes head=local_sha (876), so it carries the full sha itself.
streams.the_surface_was_measured_twice_independe: He measured the same surface with his own instruments and we agree, including on the false positives: zero file-write APIs across the nineteen; zero imports of node:child_process/http/https/net/tls/dgram/dns; his seven `exec(` matches were `RegExp.prototype.exec`, not child_process.exec - his instrument caught a method NAME; the `fetch` matches are stubs and assertions about the ABSENCE of network (`globalThis.fetch = async (...args) => { fetchCalls.push(args) }` with an assert that fetchCalls stays empty, plus `async fetch()` methods on stub objects in the two trial harnesses); and `/tmp/skipi-crewing-vault`, `/tmp/skipi-demo-a1-documents` are fixture strings inside stubbed command responses, not writes. Both of us carry the same limit: literal call sites only, so a path or host assembled from variables is invisible, and the list is a LOWER bound.
streams.the_outcome_of_this_stage_is_an_INPUT_to: Stated plainly because he asked for it plainly, and because it is the same shape as stage 6's verdict: all nineteen passing here removes a knowable reason for a refusal and grants nothing. The hook re-decides on its own stdin, in its own fresh worktree, with its own base arithmetic. A green run here is evidence; the push's verdict is the hook's; and neither my conclusion nor the coordinator's authorises a merge or a release.
